To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the local density of cosmic-ray muons is a powerful tool to study ultra-high energy cosmic ray properties, that it can be used to study the primary composition and the spectrum slope, that it can help to study the hadronic interaction at ultra-high energies, and that it can help in understanding the nature of the GZK cutoff.

(1) the muon density spectra of inclined EAS are sensitive to the primary cosmic ray spectrum and composition; (2) the muon spectra can be used for the study of hadronic interaction at the energies of 100 TeV; (3) the muon densities are sensitive to the mass of the primary particle.
the local muon spectra measured at large zenith angles are sensitive to the primary composition and spectrum slope.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the investigations of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays by the ground level measurements of the spectra local density of EAs muons at various angles.

a new experimental approach to the investigations of primary cosmic rays with energies above 10 17 eV based on the ground level measurements of the muon density in extensive air showers at various zenith angles.
a new approach to the study of ultra-high energy primary cosmic ray spectrum and composition, based on the ground level measurements of muon bundle density spectra.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
muon density measurements are very sensitive to the primary composition, and the energy spectrum, and the primary spectrum shape.
the new approach to investigations based on the ground level muon measurements is a powerful tool for studies of the ultra-high energy cosmic ray flux in wide energy range.
the muon density measurements are a promising method for studying the ultra-high energy primary cosmic ray spectrum and composition in the energy range from 1 EeV up to 10 EeV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated a new approach to the investigation of ultra-high energy CRs based on the measurements of muon bundles in inclined EAS.
we are able to study the primary spectrum in a wide energy range from ~10 15 eV to 10 20 eV, and the composition in a range from ~10 to 10 4.
the muon density spectrum in inclined showers provides a powerful tool for studying the primary spectrum, composition, and interaction features in the energy range from 3×10 16 to 3×10 ^{19} eV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the local muon densities are sensitive to the primary composition and to the features in the hadronic interaction.
the muon density spectra at large zenith angles are sensitive to the features of the primary spectrum and composition in a wide energy range.
the muon density spectra measured at different zenith angles are sensitive to the primary composition and spectrum, as well as to the characteristics of hadronic interactions.
